_comment: Data-driven regression cases for the FBR Acts corpus. status: 'active' = must pass; 'known_gap' = tracked but not counted as a regression; 'needs_review' = subjective QA note. applies_to is a substring of metadata.filename. Add cases with add_test_case.py or by hand.

cases.arg: GENERAL PROVISIONS AFFFECTING CONVEYANCES AT CUSTOMS-STATIONS
cases.description: Chapter VIII keeps the caption the BODY prints on p82 (source typo 'AFFFECTING'), not the TOC's corrected spelling; the caption reaches no leaf, so this is its only copy.

cases.arg: DISCHARGE OF CAERGO AND ENTRY INWARDS OF GOODS
cases.description: Chapter IX keeps the body caption from p86 (source typo 'CAERGO').
Chapter XII keeps the body caption 'TRANSSHIPMENT' (the TOC prints 'TRANSHIPMENT').

cases.arg: Responsibilities of person in charge or master of a conveyance, agent and owner of the conveyance
cases.description: The 2025 TOC row for 72A has the un-listed Chapter IX caption glued onto it ('... conveyance DISCHARGE OF CARGO AND ENTRY INWARDS OF GOODS'); the heading must come from the body, with the TOC text kept in toc_heading.

s.156's gridless penalty table (1,391 words, the whole conservation shortfall) must land on s.156: this edition's TOC page column runs 13 pages ahead of its own body, so the page anchor missed it and 105 of 312 sections were stubs.
s.78 must bind to its own heading on pdf 78, not to the penalty table's row serial '78. If any person on board ...' 57 pages later (what the un-drifted anchor + gap-fill did).

cases.arg: 9. Declaration of customs–ports, customs airports, etc.-
cases.description:
s.9's heading uses an EN DASH inside 'customs–ports'; the heading split must terminate at 'etc.-', not at that dash (all 20 editions cut the

to '9. Declaration of customs–' and leaked the rest into the body as a

).
The space after a superscript ordinal is drawn at the superscript's raised baseline; it must still be seen, or the 1.98pt gap glues the words into '31stday'.

s.14A's body must reach s.14A. The body prints '5[(14-A. Provision of accommodation at Customs-ports, etc.-'; the '[(' pair defeated _DOTFORM_RE (cannot step over '(') and _BRACKETPAREN_RE (needs a ')' that never comes), so the leaf shipped as a 53-char heading-only stub.
The companion half: s.14A's unbound text used to sit inside s.14 (977 chars vs a correct 508). A reader of s.14 was shown an obligation that is not in s.14.
Same '[(' pair: '24[(21A. Power to defer collection of customs-duty.-'.
The body prints '155-I.' where the TOC lists '155I'; unfolded, code_positions was keyed on '155-I' and the lookup missed, leaving a 79-char stub.
'9[194-A. Appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.-' -- 3,670 chars that used to swell s.194 to 10,212 against a correct 1,114.
The companion half for the hyphen family.

Federal Excise prints s.38 as '3[38- Alternative dispute resolution.--' -- a trailing hyphen with no suffix letter, read as code '38-'. The largest single misattribution found: 3,528 chars of the ADR provision inside s.37 in five editions.
The companion half: s.37 must drop back from 5,925 chars to its correct 2,396.

'3[18.A Special customs duty on imported goods.-' was read as code '18' -- _DOTFORM_RE's mandatory dot was satisfied by the SEPARATOR dot with the letter backtracked away, so 18A's body line was offered to section 18. _DOTSUFFIX_RE is tried first for this reason.

cases.arg: Special customs duty on imported goods
cases.description: The companion half: s.18 must drop from 3,201 chars to 2,338.

Source defect: PDF p227 opens s.204 as 'Issue of certificate and duplicate of customs document.- ...' with NO code printed (the only '204' on the page is the 9.5pt folio). Bound by the TOC-heading fallback, since no grammar change can match an absent code.
The companion half: s.203A must drop from 697 chars to 220.
